exposure: Elective induction of labor (eIOL) at 39th week of gestation
outcome: Opinion and acceptance of eIOL among low-risk pregnant women
Reasons for accepting or rejecting eIOL
Change in acceptance rates between 36 and 39 weeks of gestation
cohort: 200 low-risk pregnant women attending routine obstetrics at a tertiary hospital in Vietnam were surveyed at 36 and 39 weeks of gestation.
finding: The acceptance rate for elective induction of labor at 39 weeks decreased from 54.5% at 36 weeks to 40.1% at 39 weeks of gestation, primarily due to concerns about fetal harm and negative impacts from medical staff and relatives.
mod_finding: Acceptance of elective induction of labor at 39 weeks declined significantly closer to the due date, influenced by apprehension about risks and opinions of medical staff and relatives.
cross-section timing: Surveys conducted at 36 weeks and 39 weeks of gestation.
gest_age: Pregnant women at 36 and 39 weeks of gestation were surveyed regarding elective induction of labor at 39 weeks.
